concerns.quote: failure of the nursing home staff to recognise an acutely unwell resident
failure of the nursing home staff to undertake appropriate action when they were aware of the low blood pressure
concerns.hazard: inappropriate action after low blood pressure observed

concerns.quote: lack of ongoing training with regard to the recognition and treatment of acutely unwell residents; with reliance solely on initial nursing training
concerns.hazard: insufficient ongoing training on acute illness recognition

concerns.quote: failure of the nursing home managers to undertake an effective investigation into this incident and to take action to prevent repetition

inaccurate reporting by the nursing home managers to the Care Quality Commission (CQC) that internal protocols had been appropriately followed, when evidence given at the inquest was that this was not the case
concerns.hazard: misleading CQC report about protocol compliance

concerns.quote: lack of clarity as to the investigation that is to be undertaken by the CQC. The nursing home gave evidence that the investigation is closed, whilst the family believe it is ongoing

reports.title: Frederick Boyd: Prevention of future deaths report

concerns.quote: no clear system or expectation regarding the quality of checks on a resident who exhibited signs of being unwell
concerns.hazard: lack of clear system for quality checks on unwell resident

links.explanation: Both reports highlight problems with identifying and responding to residents who show signs of being unwell. The earlier report focuses on staff failing to recognise and act on acute illness, while the later report notes the absence of a clear system or expectation for checking such residents.
links.earlier_quote: (1) failure of the nursing home staff to recognise an acutely unwell resident;
links.later_quote: The inquest heard evidence that there was no clear system or expectation regarding the quality of checks on a resident who exhibited signs of being unwell.
